translationRepairs: In the seventh year of Tianfu, after Taizu took Yan, he received appointment as vice director of punishments in the Ministry of Works and as magistrate of Anchang in Jinzhou; he was later made attendant of the heir apparent and compiler at the Historiography Institute, and for distinguished service on campaign was promoted to vice director of the palace workshops.

In the seventh year of Tianfu, after Taizu took Yan, he received appointment as vice director of the Dugong (Punishments) Bureau of the Department of State Affairs and as magistrate of Anchang in Jinzhou; he was later made court diarist and compiler at the Historiography Institute, and for distinguished service on campaign was promoted to vice director of the palace workshops.

尚書都官員外郎 names the Dugong bureau under the Department of State Affairs; the Chinese has no 工部 so 'Ministry of Works' is an insertion. 起居郎 is the court diarist recording the emperor's activities (起居), not an attendant of the heir apparent.

In the seventh year of Tianfu, when the Taizu entered Yan, he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments in the Ministry of Works and magistrate of Anchang in Jinzhou; he was successively promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, served as compiler in the Historiography Institute, and for meritorious service on campaign was made Vice Director of the Palace Workshops.

In the seventh year of Tianfu, when the Taizu entered Yan, he was appointed Vice Director of the Dugong (Punishments) Bureau of the Department of State Affairs and magistrate of Anchang in Jinzhou; he was successively promoted to Court Diarist, served as compiler in the Historiography Institute, and for meritorious service on campaign was made Vice Director of the Palace Workshops.
尚書都官員外郎 contains no 工部 ('Ministry of Works'); 都官 is the punishments-related bureau under 尚書. 起居郎 is the court diarist (起居 = the emperor's daily activities), not Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

Kong Fan, styled Wenlao, was the forty-ninth-generation descendant of Confucius; he was the son of Duancao, younger brother of Duan You, who had inherited the Song enfeoffment as gentleman for attendance.

Kong Fan, styled Wenlao, was the forty-ninth-generation descendant of Confucius; he was the son of Duancao, younger brother of Duanyou, who had inherited the Song enfeoffment as gentleman for attendance.
端友 and 端操 are parallel given names of brothers; romanize consistently as Duanyou (not 'Duan You', which reads as surname + given name).

Liu Yu levied a ten-percent tax on the people under the name of restoring an ancient practice, but in truth it was heavy extraction. Punishments were severe, and officials abused their power to commit abuse.

Liu Yu levied a ten-percent tax on the people under the name of restoring an ancient practice, but in truth it was heavy extraction. Punishments were severe and urgent, and officials exploited connections to commit abuses.
吏夤緣為暴 means officials used connections/opportunities to act oppressively; 'abused their power to commit abuse' is tautological and drops 夤緣; 嚴急 is 'severe and urgent'.
He was convicted of using personal influence to reduce charges against an old acquaintance in a treason case, flogged forty strokes, and demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Taide Army.
He was convicted of interceding on behalf of an old acquaintance charged with a sexual offense, flogged forty strokes, and demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Taiding Army.
奸罪 denotes an illicit-sex offense, not treason (反/叛); 請囑 is interceding by request. 泰定軍 is Taiding, not Taide.
When Hailing took the throne he was summoned as signing secretary of the Huizheng Court, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and tutor to the heir apparent.
When Hailing took the throne he was summoned as signing secretary of the Huizheng Court, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and supervisor of the household of the heir apparent.
太子詹事 is the supervisor (chief steward) of the heir apparent's household, not a tutor; tutoring posts are 太子太傅/少師 etc.
When Chief Minister Shi Kui retired, the emperor asked him, "Who can take your place?"
When Chief Minister Shi Ju retired, the emperor asked him, "Who can take your place?"
石琚: 琚 is read jū, so the name is Shi Ju, not 'Shi Kui'.
When the post of tutor to the heir apparent fell vacant, the chief ministers again recommended Boxiong.
When the post of supervisor of the heir apparent's household fell vacant, the chief ministers again recommended Boxiong.
太子詹事 is the supervisor of the heir apparent's household, not a tutor.
Thereupon he was made tutor to the heir apparent while retaining his remonstrating post.
Thereupon he was made supervisor of the heir apparent's household while retaining his remonstrating post.
太子詹事 is the supervisor of the heir apparent's household, not a tutor.
His son Ershi entered service when Zhangzong took the throne as keeper of seals and treasures and rose to left remonstrating grand master.
His son Ershi: when Zhangzong took the throne, Ershi was made keeper of seals and treasures, and he rose through office to left remonstrating grand master.
Current wording lets 'as keeper of seals and treasures' attach to Zhangzong; 以為符寶典書 has Ershi as the appointee.

After mourning his father he was recalled to serve as vice director and then director in the right office, then as chancellor of the directorate of education and vice minister of rites, and he joined Chen Daren in editing the History of Liao.

After mourning his father he was recalled to serve as vice director and then director in the right office, then as chancellor of the directorate of education and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and he joined Chen Daren in editing the History of Liao.
太常少卿 is vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (太常寺), not 'vice minister of rites' (禮部侍郎).

In the Da'an era, as Grand Councillor Dujishi Zhong and Vice Grand Councillor Chengyu held a frontier provincial commission, Han served as director in the left and right departments, but their counsels did not align.

In the Da'an era, as Grand Councillor Duji Sizhong and Vice Grand Councillor Chengyu held a frontier provincial commission, Han served as director in the left and right departments, but their counsels did not align.
獨吉思忠 is the clan name Duji (獨吉) plus the given name Sizhong (思忠); 'Dujishi Zhong' misdivides it.
Censors Gao Kui and Liu Yuangui recommended Tianchong, praising his public diligence, sharp intelligence, and capacity to settle and reassure the people.
Investigating censors Gao Kui and Liu Yuangui recommended Tianchong among twenty men as publicly diligent, sharp and able, fit to settle and reassure the people.
舉天寵二十人 names Tianchong as one of twenty men recommended; the current wording drops the twenty.
He received the posthumous title Chundu.
He received the posthumous title Chunsu.
純肅 is romanized Chunsu; 'Chundu' misreads 肅.
